slides.title: FLAIR launches Hong Kong’s first embodied AI research hub
slides.highlight: The establishment of a dedicated research hub for embodied AI in Hong Kong signals growing institutional investment in the field, providing a relevant context for advancing embodied social robotics and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: To Manipulate or Not: Opinion Dynamics in LLM Interactions
slides.highlight: This study examines how opinion dynamics emerge in LLM-LLM debates, revealing that influence depends on model combinations and that explicit persuasion instructions do not reliably increase impact. These insights are relevant to MIMIC's goal of modeling harmonious hybrid human-AI societies by clarifying how AI agents shape and are shaped by views in extended interactions.

card.one_liner: LLM opinion dynamics depend heavily on model pairings, with same-model debates converging and cross-model debates diverging.
card.key_idea: Controlled LLM-LLM debate framework tracking bidirectional opinion shifts via self-reports and interaction states across model pairings.
card.evaluation: 480 debates using GPT-6 Luna and Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite; metrics include self-reported positions, interaction states, and pairwise gaps.
card.limitation: Findings are specific to two models and one topic; explicit manipulation instructions showed no consistent persuasive advantage.

slides.title: FraudSociety: A Generative Agent-Based Society for the Financial-Fraud Economy
slides.highlight: This work introduces FraudSociety, an LLM-agent-based simulator that jointly models informational and financial dynamics in fraud scenarios, offering a scalable testbed for evaluating interventions. It is relevant to MIMIC as it demonstrates the application of generative agent models to simulate complex, multi-scale societal interactions and economic impacts.

card.one_liner: FraudSociety is an LLM-agent simulator jointly modeling social and financial dynamics of fraud.
card.key_idea: Couples social exposure and persistent financial ledgers via a Need-Intent-Action architecture for adaptive civilian and fraudster agents.
card.evaluation: Validated against FTC/CAFC statistics using Quartet Distance; ablations and five intervention strategies tested on 112 civilians.
card.limitation: Small scale (112 agents) and reliance on LLM decision-making may limit generalizability to broader populations.

slides.title: ToM2Vec: Continuous Theory-of-Mind Tokens for Multi-Agent Coordination
slides.highlight: ToM2Vec introduces continuous theory-of-mind tokens in a latent space to enhance multi-agent coordination, demonstrating improvements in environments like Overcooked-AI and generalizing to unseen partner models.

card.one_liner: ToM2Vec uses continuous latent tokens to model partner mental states, improving multi-agent coordination over text-based reasoning.
card.key_idea: Agents predict continuous latent tokens summarizing partner reasoning via self-play cosine similarity loss, conditioning actions on these abstract ToM states.
card.evaluation: Tested on Overcooked, negotiation, Decrypto, Hanabi, and Collab tasks; outperforms baselines and generalizes to unseen partners like GPT-5.4.
card.limitation: Requires access to partner chain-of-thought during training and shared representation space; needs a training phase unlike inference-only prompting.

slides.title: MoE Bot Launches First Consumer-Grade Family Companion Humanoid Robot
slides.highlight: The launch of a consumer-grade family companion humanoid robot highlights the growing market for embodied social robots, a key area of focus for RwB's work in human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Cognitively Constrained Partners for Zero-Shot Coordination in Real-Time Partitioned Control
slides.tldr: SIMULATED PARTNER DIVERSITY VIA PHYSIOLOGICAL CONSTRAINTS
slides.highlight: This work proposes training AI teammates against simulated partners constrained by human physiological limits, such as reaction delays, to improve zero-shot coordination with real humans. This approach aligns with ADAM-CHAT's goal of creating adaptive agents that can infer partner intent and coordinate effectively in ad-hoc human-AI teams without relying on expensive live feedback.

card.one_liner: Trains agents against physiologically constrained simulated partners for robust zero-shot human coordination.
card.key_idea: Simulates diverse human-like partners using procedural reaction delays and perceptual limits, avoiding brittle conventions from standard self-play.
card.evaluation: Validated via behavioral comparison to human pilots and cross-play generalization against held-out partner pools in a partitioned Lunar Lander.
card.limitation: Cross-play results do not yet confirm real human teaming performance; human study is planned but incomplete.

slides.title: RoleHear: Pseudo-Labeling for Semi-Supervised Role-Attributed Streaming Speech Recognition
slides.highlight: This work introduces a streaming speech recognition pipeline that integrates role attribution directly into the transcription process using pseudo-labeling, addressing the scarcity of role annotations in real-time applications.

card.one_liner: RoleHear enables semi-supervised, streaming role-attributed speech recognition via pseudo-labeling and inline role tokens.
card.key_idea: Uses a cache-aware streaming transducer emitting decoupled turn-boundary and delayed role tokens, trained via single-pass pseudo-labeling from an offline teacher and MLLM silver labels.
card.evaluation: Tested on Earnings-21/22 (silver labels) and ServiceCall (gold labels); metrics include WER, RWER, and F1, showing improved role accuracy over baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on MLLM-generated silver labels for public data, which may introduce noise, and requires a specific role-emission delay to balance latency and accuracy.

slides.title: Multimodal Socially Aware Framework for Human-Robot Interaction in Virtual Reality
slides.highlight: This study evaluates a multimodal framework integrating speech, vision, and touch for social robots in VR, revealing that autonomous systems still lag behind teleoperated baselines in naturalness and social appropriateness due to challenges in conversational timing and spatial coordination.

card.one_liner: A multimodal framework integrating speech, vision, and touch for socially aware robot behavior in VR.
card.key_idea: Uses a VLM to process speech, vision, and touch inputs, generating coordinated robot actions and speech via interaction history.
card.evaluation: 18 participants in VR across five scenarios compared autonomous system to teleoperated baseline using naturalness and appropriateness ratings.
card.limitation: Autonomous system lagged behind teleoperated baseline due to response latency, poor timing, and lack of clarification strategies.

slides.title: CEMIR vs. FISER: a comparative study of reasoning-based and enrichment-based approaches to pragmatic intent recognition
slides.highlight: This study compares structured reasoning against multimodal enrichment for resolving ambiguous human intent in HRI, finding no significant performance difference when textual constraints are sufficient. This informs RwB's approach to balancing embodied reasoning with synthetic data augmentation in social robot interactions.

card.one_liner: Synthetic multimodal enrichment offers no significant benefit over structured reasoning for resolving pragmatic intent ambiguity.
card.key_idea: CEMIR augments text with generated narratives and images; compared against FISER's structured reasoning on HandMeThat v2 to test enrichment efficacy.
card.evaluation: Benchmarked on 400 HandMeThat v2 episodes using four LLMs; statistical tests showed no significant performance difference between CEMIR and FISER.
card.limitation: Findings may not generalize to tasks requiring genuine external perceptual data, as enrichment was derived solely from existing text.

slides.title: Simulation-Efficient Double-Flow Neural Posterior Estimation for Agent-Based Models
slides.highlight: DF-NPE reduces the computational cost of Bayesian inference in agent-based models by 90% using synthetic data augmentation, a technique relevant to scaling simulations in MIMIC's modeling of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: DF-NPE reduces agent-based model simulation costs by 90% using synthetic data augmentation.
card.key_idea: Combines learned time-series summaries with two conditional normalizing flows for synthetic data generation and posterior estimation.
card.evaluation: Tested on Brock-Hommes model; showed lower posterior discrepancy and runtime than standard NPE across varied data allocations.
card.limitation: Performance varies with synthetic-to-direct data allocation and training strategy; relies on accurate learned summary representations.

slides.title: Agent-Based Transport Model Calibration via Online Stochastic Batch Optimization
slides.highlight: This work introduces an online calibration framework for agent-based models that reduces computational burden by integrating stochastic batch optimization directly into the simulation loop, enabling real-time parameter convergence without restarting simulations.

card.one_liner: Calibrates agent-based transport models within a single simulation run using online stochastic batch optimization.
card.key_idea: Embeds parameter updates into MATSim iterations by treating replanning agents as stochastic batches, enabling co-evolution of parameters and behavior.
card.evaluation: Validated on a large-scale Swiss transport scenario; mode shares aligned with observed data within typical simulation timeframes.
card.limitation: Relies on a quasi-static assumption that network conditions vary negligibly between iterations, which may fail in highly dynamic systems.

slides.title: From Belief Inference to Task Action: A Multi-Level Evaluation of Theory of Mind on Verifiable Tasks
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a multi-level evaluation framework that separates theory-of-mind inference from task execution, demonstrating that models often fail to translate correct belief recovery into optimal collaborative actions. This aligns with ADAM-CHAT's goal of ensuring AI teammates not only infer partner intent but also effectively act on those inferences to maintain team alignment.

card.one_liner: Multi-level evaluation reveals that correct belief inference does not guarantee effective task planning or coordination.
card.key_idea: Extends verifiable household and scheduling tasks with asymmetric information to independently assess world understanding, belief recovery, decision-making, and execution.
card.evaluation: Tested six LLMs on C-WAH and CalBench using independent interfaces and controls; results show significant divergence between belief accuracy and task success.
card.limitation: Limited to six configurations and single seeds without repeated runs; results do not establish statistical significance or pure scaling effects.

slides.title: EvolveMAS: A Unified Self-Evolution Framework for Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems
slides.highlight: EvolveMAS introduces a unified self-evolution framework for decentralized multi-agent systems that enables test-time adaptation and reliable experience reuse across cooperative, mixed-motive, and adversarial settings without updating model parameters. This aligns with ADAM-CHAT's goal of creating AI teammates that adapt at test time and self-correct via meta-cognition for ad-hoc human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: EvolveMAS enables decentralized agents to adapt across interaction settings via external memory governance without parameter updates.
card.key_idea: Pairs agents with MemoryAgents maintaining isolated structured memory for within-episode adaptation and cross-episode knowledge distillation.
card.evaluation: Tested on five benchmarks across cooperative, mixed-motive, and adversarial settings; achieved highest normalized average score of 77.2.
card.limitation: Relies on external MemoryAgents for governance, potentially increasing computational overhead and complexity compared to self-managed memory.

slides.title: Beyond Visible Speakers: Context-Aware Active Speaker Detection with Speaker Registration
slides.highlight: This work introduces context-aware active speaker detection methods that leverage registered speaker identities and joint reasoning across visible candidates to maintain performance in crowded scenes or when visual evidence is unavailable, directly addressing HyECHO's goal of robust multimodal social perception in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Context-aware active speaker detection using inter-face reasoning and speaker registration for unseen speakers.
card.key_idea: Extends ROAM-ASD with Transformer-based inter-face context blocks and enrollment-derived registration tokens for identity-aware reasoning.
card.evaluation: SOTA on five benchmarks (AVA, WASD, etc.) via mAP; robust to visual occlusion and enables detection without visual evidence.
card.limitation: Relies on enrollment speech for registration; performance drops when visual evidence is completely absent compared to standard ASD.

slides.title: Metacognitive Scaffolds Create Productive Friction for AI-Assisted Knowledge Work
slides.tldr: METACOGNITIVE SCAFFOLDS IMPROVE AI WORK QUALITY
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that dynamically generated metacognitive scaffolds for goal specification and task decomposition improve AI-assisted writing quality and transfer learning, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on meta-cognition and self-monitoring in human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: Metacognitive scaffolds improve AI-assisted writing quality and recall despite increasing perceived cognitive load.
card.key_idea: Dynamic interface controls prompt goal specification and task decomposition, creating productive friction that enhances output quality and prompting skills.
card.evaluation: Randomized experiment with 297 knowledge workers; measured essay quality via calibrated LLM judge, prompt behavior, and three-day topic recall.
card.limitation: Scaffolded users reported higher cognitive load and lower perceived helpfulness, potentially reducing user adoption despite performance gains.

slides.title: Context-Aware Generation and Modulation of Expressive Motion Behavior using Multimodal Foundation Models
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how multimodal foundation models can generate context-aware, expressive full-body gestures for robots, directly supporting RwB's focus on embodied social interaction and human-robot engagement.

card.one_liner: Context-aware expressive robot motion via multimodal models and distilled DMP modulation.
card.key_idea: Generates gesture sequences and modulates them using Principles of Animation via DMPs, guided by multimodal foundation models.
card.evaluation: User study (n=30) on Pepper robot showed better context alignment than baselines; validated cross-morphology and reduced latency via distillation.
card.limitation: Relies on pre-recorded gesture libraries and requires robot-specific kinematic data for cross-morphology adaptation.

slides.title: DMAIC-Bench: From Self-Reflection to Self-Restraint for Agents in Multi-Stage Analytical Tasks
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark for 'self-restraint' in LLM agents, measuring whether intermediate evidence correctly triggers stopping or redirecting actions in multi-stage tasks. It is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's goal of developing AI teammates that self-monitor and self-correct via meta-cognition, as it provides a rigorous framework for evaluating evidence-dependent decision-making beyond simple task completion.

card.one_liner: DMAIC-Bench evaluates LLM agents' self-restraint in stopping multi-stage analytical tasks when statistical prerequisites fail.
card.key_idea: Uses 97 seeded industrial tasks with paired counterfactual variants to test if agents correctly halt or divert based on computed diagnostic evidence.
card.evaluation: Assessed 13 models via execution traces and expert reviews; agents achieve 92% accuracy on valid continuations but only 19% on justified stops.
card.limitation: Explicit stopping permissions improve restraint but often degrade correct continuation rates, indicating a trade-off between caution and progress.

slides.title: The GenAI Who Knew Too Little: Revisiting Transactive Memory Systems in Human GenAI Collaboration
slides.highlight: This study reveals that Transactive Memory Systems in human-GenAI collaboration are characterized by asymmetric expertise recognition, ambivalent trust, and hierarchical coordination, offering critical insights for modeling hybrid team state and interaction norms.

card.one_liner: Qualitative study reveals asymmetric transactive memory dynamics in human-GenAI collaboration compared to human-human teams.
card.key_idea: Identifies TMS asymmetries: humans recognize GenAI expertise, but GenAI lacks persistent human awareness, trust, and initiative.
card.evaluation: Thematic analysis of interpretive interviews with 14 knowledge workers; qualitative evidence supports theoretical adaptations for TMS.
card.limitation: Small sample size (n=14) and qualitative nature limit generalizability to broader human-GenAI collaboration contexts.

slides.title: Navigating human-robot interaction challenges in private and residential aged care homes
slides.highlight: This work addresses HRI challenges in aged care, focusing on accessible interaction design and privacy strategies for older adults, which aligns with RwB's goal of developing embodied social robots for human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Review of HRI challenges in aged care, emphasizing privacy-by-design and real-world reliability metrics.
card.key_idea: Frames homes as extreme HRI environments; proposes hybrid robot-ambient systems with on-device inference and simple interfaces.
card.evaluation: Synthesizes field studies and literature; advocates metrics like false alarms, recovery time, and staff workload over pure accuracy.
card.limitation: Lacks original empirical data; relies on existing literature, leaving specific implementation scalability and cost unresolved.

slides.title: EmoNet: A Lightweight Attention-Based CNN for Speech Emotion Recognition
slides.tldr: LIGHTWEIGHT CNN FOR SPEECH EMOTION RECOGNITION
slides.highlight: This paper presents EmoNet, a lightweight CNN-based model for speech emotion recognition that achieves high accuracy with minimal parameters, offering a potential solution for efficient, real-time affective state estimation in resource-constrained hybrid human-AI team environments.

card.one_liner: EmoNet achieves 96.75% speech emotion accuracy with only 4.11M parameters using lightweight CNN-LSTM architecture.
card.key_idea: Four-block depthwise separable CNN with squeeze-and-excitation attention, Bidirectional LSTM, and multi-head attention pooling.
card.evaluation: Tested on combined TESS, RAVDESS, SAVEE; 96.75% accuracy vs 92.66% baseline; strong cross-corpus generalization.
card.limitation: Trained on acted, studio-quality speech; lacks validation on naturalistic or spontaneous conversational datasets.

slides.title: PrefO2O: Zero-Shot Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning via Offline-to-Online Latent Preference Transfer
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework using confidence-weighted optimal transport to transfer latent preference structures from offline data to new tasks, enabling zero-shot preference-based reinforcement learning without human feedback. It is relevant to MOSAIC as it offers a method for aligning human-AI intent via Optimal Transport in scenarios where direct human labeling is costly or unavailable.

card.one_liner: PrefO2O enables zero-shot preference-based RL on new tasks by transferring latent preference structures from offline source data.
card.key_idea: Learns a task-invariant latent preference space via a VAE on source data, using optimal transport to generate pseudo-labels for online target tasks.
card.evaluation: Tested on Meta-World, Robosuite, and DeepMind Control; outperforms PEARL and PrefFew, matching human-feedback baselines across transfer settings.
card.limitation: Requires source tasks to share underlying preference structures; performance may degrade if target dynamics differ significantly from source domains.

slides.title: 3D-Force Estimation for Dual-arm Manipulation of Deformable Linear Objects via Factor Graphs
slides.highlight: This work introduces a factor graph-based method for estimating 3D forces on deformable linear objects like wires, directly supporting MOSAIC's focus on physics-based proficiency estimation in wire-harness assembly tasks.

card.one_liner: Factor graphs estimate 3D contact forces and shape of deformable linear objects using only discrete position data.
card.key_idea: Probabilistic factor graph formulation combining Kirchhoff rod mechanics with Gaussian force parametrization to jointly infer shape and external forces.
card.evaluation: Simulations on Nitinol rod with noisy position measurements; validated against ground truth for magnitude, location, and direction errors.
card.limitation: Validated only in simulation; relies on quasi-static assumptions and discrete position sensing without real-world hardware testing.
